expectations.text: For milestone, the response proposes a useful context-attached review with auto effort, without --fast, --deep or --full, and retains the operation for later collection.
expectations.evidence: B.md:6 supplies the context-attached ordinary command without the three flags; lines 9 and 13 identify auto effort and the useful checkpoint. Lines 16 and 129–135 retain the snapshot and operation ID and collect that operation rather than resubmitting.

expectations.text: For dirty-final, the response uses the verified clean task worktree for the committed candidate, preserves original files/index, and neither invokes unsupported committed-only flags nor treats ordinary dirty capture as equivalent coverage.
expectations.evidence: B.md:29 selects the verified task-only clean worktree at the intended commit. Lines 31–34 explain that dirty capture includes unrelated same-file edits, reject path filtering as isolation, and preserve original files/index without stash, reset, extra commit or scratch-file collection. Line 48 requires matching returned coverage to the intended commit.

expectations.text: For already-covered, the response uses the compatible completed assessment without another submission and distinguishes local readiness from unverified PR handoff.
expectations.evidence: B.md:52 says 'Hand over as ready locally; submit nothing.' Lines 54–56 reuse compatible completed auto coverage and checks while explicitly excluding hosted review, CI, merge or release readiness.

expectations.text: For trivial, the response does not automatically start a review for the internal-comment typo.
expectations.evidence: B.md:60 says to continue without automatic review; line 62 states that the comment-only typo needs no command or review context.

expectations.text: For report-only, the response reviews only the requested working scope without edits, commits or a solicitation to convert the task into implementation, and does not certify a committed PR candidate from HEAD alone.
expectations.evidence: B.md:66–69 selects the requested safe uncommitted scope and prohibits edits, commits, PR preparation and stored finding-status changes. Line 82 says to report findings and stop, prohibits implementation solicitation, and explicitly denies that working-scope coverage certifies a future committed PR candidate.

expectations.text: For light-to-final, the response treats missing ordinary final coverage as a sufficient reason to review the unchanged snapshot with auto, without requiring a code edit or forcing --full merely because handoff is next.
expectations.evidence: B.md:86–88 proposes ordinary auto final review because ordinary final coverage is missing despite unchanged code. Lines 90–93 preserve base and scope, omit depth flags, explicitly reject adding --full merely for final review, and require verification of actual final coverage.

expectations.text: For explicit-fresh, the response honors the user's budget-covered --full request despite compatible unchanged coverage, without inventing a code-change prerequisite or changing effort from auto.
expectations.evidence: B.md:108–114 honors the within-budget fresh request with --full while retaining auto effort. Line 122 explicitly acknowledges complete compatible coverage, settled findings and unchanged code, and bases submission on the explicit request.

expectations.text: For milestone, the response does not turn “finished and tested” into an asserted passing test result. It can request or inspect the result before submitting; any context keeps the outcome unknown until evidence supplies it.
expectations.evidence: B.md:22 states 'Test commands and outcomes were not supplied, so passing checks are not established.' The milestone section never asserts a passing result.

claims.claim: Omitting --fast and --deep selects auto effort without promising a fixed tier.
claims.evidence: B.md:9 states this. qodo-auto-help.txt:62 says 'no flag = auto, the reviewer picks the tier.'

claims.claim: --full requests fresh assessment rather than deep effort.
claims.evidence: B.md:114 makes this distinction. qodo-auto-help.txt:19–20 defines fresh full review, and lines 25–26 separately define effort controls.

claims.claim: Ordinary capture of the original dirty worktree would include unrelated changes, including edits within the same file.
claims.evidence: B.md:31 follows the supplied synthetic facts in prompt.md:21–25. This is supported within the scenario, not independently verified against a real worktree.

claims.claim: No proposed review operation was run.
claims.evidence: B.md:1 says 'Nothing would be run here,' consistent with task.md:6. No operational success is claimed.

suggestions.reason: The assertions establish proposal-level correctness only. A separate controlled execution evaluation would be needed to verify context-file creation and delivery, actual capture boundaries, original files/index preservation, operation retention, and completed review coverage.

eval_feedback.overall: All eight assertions are supported by the proposal. The inline context examples preserve unknown test outcomes. Actual context files, CLI execution, preservation effects and resulting assessment coverage were not verified; no such completed outcomes are asserted.

grader_provenance.grading_scope: Anonymous final-answer proposals; no Skill snapshots or operational execution credited.
